uncertainties: Research cutoff 30 September 2026; accessed 1 October. The historical vessel relationship is used solely for identity and omitted from both biographies.

Creation-sector materiality is a reasoned inference from personally owned, sustained investment operations, corroborated across contemporary accounts. The customer's ships and fund assets are not personal holdings. No personal net-worth amount is proposed.

The 2013 transaction involved two owners jointly selling 80 percent. Consideration was used for liabilities and contingent-liability release; it is not treated as an individual cash windfall or proof of current assets.

Earlier independent property activity does not automatically make Real Estate the original fortune sector. No evidence established its personal materiality relative to the defining financial platform.

Current origin-sector fallback is deliberate. XING's historical role endpoints are self-reported; CompanyHouse reproduces dated register notices rather than constituting an official register extract. Those notices corroborate closure, not insolvency or exhausted personal wealth. Current portfolio composition remains unknown.

Founder and Investor are the strongest current-role alternatives, but neither a past founder label nor miscellaneous director appointments identifies an ongoing principal economic interest. No passive delegation is inferred from silence.

All seven supported personal profile types were checked: LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter/X, Youtube, TikTok and Personal Website. No eligible personal profile reached verification. TikTok direct access was restricted; indexed discovery produced no verified match. Club accounts are organisational, not personal.

LinkedIn profiles for the Intrum lawyer in Hannover, a Berlin photographer, a Stadtwerke lawyer and a Rhenus logistics executive were rejected. The photographer's personal website and a Notzingen namesake born in 1983 were also rejected. XING matches the business chronology but is not an eligible input social type.
Old personal and Lexington domains did not yield a verifiable live public profile. The closed companies' domains and the sailing club are not proposed as current personal company links.

Public age and register-intermediary leads suggest a 1962 birth year, but no sufficiently strong explicit personal birth record was verified. No exact date, birthplace, middle names or secondary nationality is proposed; age alone is not converted to a birth year.

Primary programme accounts attribute development jointly and identify public grants, bank support and private donors. The biographies do not attribute all funding, design or implementation personally to König.

Full relevant business and association bodies were read. The DSV article was read via public HTML extraction after web-reader failure. The signed König/Jürgensen contribution was read in its complete indexed section; the direct paginated NRV page also contains unrelated club material. WELT contributes only a bounded identity fact. Source derivations remain below each source's 200-word limit and the WELT 100-word limit, counting metadata and prose together.

Asset management and Competitive sailing are the minimum useful active tags for separate professional and public-sport dimensions. Shipping exposure through client funds does not justify assigning personal Shipping ownership or an unapproved concept.

biography.plain_text: Tobias König is a German investment entrepreneur who founded Hamburg fund manager König & Cie. in 1999. Initially specialising in ship funds, the firm extended into property and private equity. He also served on Marenave's management board and ran a separate property business, alongside a sustained public role in competitive sailing.

long_biography.plain_text:
Investment entrepreneur Tobias König helped develop an inclusive sailing programme at Hamburg's Norddeutscher Regatta Verein with Sven Jürgensen and experienced disabled sailors. The club's accessible harbour and adaptable boats supported training and racing together. Public funding, bank support and private donations financed the new facilities, which opened in 2022.

König encouraged clubs to pool resources rather than each trying to provide every facility. His proposal allowed clubs to specialise and share access, extending opportunities beyond those able to fund comprehensive adaptations themselves. He also chaired the German S/V14 class association, formed to connect sailors and clubs around a boat designed for mixed-ability crews.
